newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hog prices mixed on snow-dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hog prices mixed on snow-dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices early Monday were mixed, depending on weather-related disruptions in hog marketings, livestock dealers said.

Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold fully steady early at $52.50-$53.00 per cwt in the country and $53.50 to $54.50 at plants. Blowing snow in the upper half of Iowa and southern Minnesota was making travel difficult, which could result in lighter hog marketings and firmer prices as the day unfolds, sources there said.
Illinois hogs were trading steady to up $0.50 at $53.00-$54.00 in the country and $54.00-$55.00 at plants.
Slippery roads in southern Illinois was restricting hog movement and supporting prices, sources there said.
However, Indiana hogs sold steady to $0.50 lower following brisk hog marketings early, with top prices at $51.00 to $51.50 in the country $52.00 to $52.50 at plants.

Ohio dealers said ice and snow in the southern part of the state was keeping hog runs light and resulting in steady to $0.50 higher sales at $51.00 to $52.00 in the country and up to $54.00 at plants.
An overnight fire at Excel Corp's Ottumwa, Iowa pork plant will keep the plant closed at least until Tuesday.
A company official said it had not been determined how long the plant will be closed and hogs normally processed at the plant will be shipped to Excel plants in Marshall, Mo., and Beardstown, Ill.
